installation_plan:
Dependencies, HTTPS, the strfry service and two timers will be installed/configured.
Files: /etc/caddy, /etc/strfry, /usr/local/bin/strfry, /usr/local/libexec,
/etc/systemd/system, /var/lib/strfry and /var/lib/neighbors-relay-setup.
Existing relays are not upgraded; swap is not created; SSH and firewall are not changed.
caddy_restored: Caddy rejected the configuration. The package-default file was restored; the relay remains on loopback.
build_progress: [2/5] Building sources; this may take several minutes…
caddy_key_failed: Caddy key verification failed. The repository was not added; do not bypass the fingerprint check.
https_progress: [5/5] Checking HTTPS; obtaining a certificate may take several minutes…
nip11_mismatch: HTTPS responded, but NIP-11 does not match the relay configuration.
metrics_exposed: /metrics must return 404 through the HTTPS endpoint.
ready:
Ready: wss://{v0}/relay
Services, local HTTPS and blocked /metrics were checked.
Check external reachability and X25519MLKEM768 from another machine:
  OPENSSL=/path/to/openssl-3.5+ sh scripts/check-pq-tls.sh {v1}
Use the app release with the relay page; authentication is handled by the app automatically.
https_not_ready: Services are installed, but HTTPS is not ready. Check A/AAAA, TCP 80/443 reachability and Caddy logs. Then run sh setup.sh --check.
description: Local relay setup wizard for clean Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64.
binary_help: local binary instead of the bundled file
plan_help: check prerequisites and show the plan without writing files
yes_help: execute an explicitly specified plan without interactive confirmation
check_help: check an installed relay; do not install anything
check_conflict: --check cannot be combined with installation options.
domain_required: Provide --domain or run the wizard in an interactive terminal.
source_binary_conflict: --binary and --sha256 cannot be used with --mode source.
confirmation_required: For noninteractive installation, provide --yes after reviewing --plan.
already_running: Another setup wizard is already running.
no_changes: System changes have not started; --check does not install anything either.
recovery:
Package changes are not rolled back automatically. If installation has started, do not delete the database or rerun the wizard blindly.
Diagnostics: systemctl status caddy strfry --no-pager; journalctl -u caddy -n 50 --no-pager
After fixing DNS/ports: sudo sh setup.sh --check
interrupted: Stopped by the user. If installation had started, keep the output for diagnosis.
mode_help: install a binary or compile from source
auth_help: require NIP-42 for reading private envelopes (needs a compatible custom-relay client)
auth_plan: AUTH enabled: kind 1059 can be read only by an authenticated involved key. Writes remain public. The relay learns a verified inbox-key/connection link; Caddy sees IPs. Gateway and courier modes are unavailable on custom relays. Use only after installing a client with NIP-42 support.
public_plan: AUTH disabled: anyone knowing the address can read ciphertext and visible tags or submit events.
auth_template_mismatch: AUTH configuration template changed; refusing to start with unexpected restrictions.
config_help: values file with KEY=VALUE lines (DOMAIN, AUTH, LANGUAGE, MODE, NAME, CONTACT, TLS_TIMEOUT); command-line options take precedence
contact_help: abuse contact shown in NIP-11, an e-mail or URL (optional)
config_unknown_key: Values file: unknown key {v0}. Allowed: DOMAIN, AUTH, LANGUAGE, MODE, NAME, CONTACT, TLS_TIMEOUT.
config_domain_missing: Fill in DOMAIN in {v0}, for example DOMAIN=relay.example.org.
invalid_name: NAME: up to 64 printable characters without quotes or backslashes.
invalid_contact: CONTACT: up to 200 printable characters without quotes, backslashes or spaces.
summary:
==============================================================
Relay address for the app:  wss://{v0}/relay
In the app: Neighbors chat → settings → Internet → Relay → add this address.
Neighbors reach each other over the Internet only through the same address.
Gateways and couriers are unavailable on your own relay; Bluetooth nearby works as before.
{v1}
Check later:    sudo sh setup.sh --check
Saved settings: /var/lib/neighbors-relay-setup/state.json
==============================================================
summary_auth_on: Authentication: ON (NIP-42). There is no password, login or list of allowed keys: the app proves its own inbox key for this relay automatically. Private envelopes can be read only by the app they are addressed to. Anyone can still submit envelopes, and the operator still sees addresses, times and IPs.
summary_auth_off: Authentication: OFF. Anyone who knows the address can read the encrypted envelopes and their tags; message content stays end-to-end encrypted. To restrict reads, install a fresh relay with AUTH=yes or see the README, Authentication.
